doc.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Editing interviews for his books
summary: Dance explains he left out questions in his books and ordered the musicians' material, disliking question-and-answer formats.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When you wrote these books, the Count Basie and, the conversations you had with the musicians, I notice your questions aren’t here. You just left out your questions and basically let them talk. Was there much editing you had to do for this work?

Well the editing had to do, you have to put the material in an order. You know, because you sit for two hours talking to a guy, while he remembers something, he says oh but— so you’ve got to bring this back. And I think the interviews which are question and answer are very tiring to read. I think the interviewer should be out of it as much as possible. I think it’s a waste of space, and the reader’s attention really.
